done_when: A git-ignored forge.local.toml beside forge.toml, read from the main checkout so every task and fix worktree of that clone uses it, overrides only which tools run work, the worker split and the model and effort per kind of work; Forge refuses any other key in it; new and upgraded repos ignore the file in git; forge next and forge doctor show which file each of those settings came from

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The required source display is incomplete in `forge next`: it labels a ready task with `forge.local.toml` only when local `tools` or `workers` is present, and never shows where its model or effort came from. With a local model-only override, `forge next` shows no local source. It can also label a Codex choice as local when local `workers = "claude"` is overridden by shared `tools = "codex"`. The Done-when requirement asks `forge next` to show which file each setting came from.
findings.title: Not done: A git-ignored forge.local.toml beside forge.toml, read from the main checkout so every task and fix worktree of that clone uses it

findings.body: Raise: Test. The worker execution proof writes a local file containing `workers` and a build model, but no `tools` value. The other test writes local `tools = "claude"` only after the work step and checks doctor and sync, never worker execution. A broken local `tools` override at `forge work` would leave every named proof passing, although choosing which tool runs work is a Done-when behavior.
findings.title: Not done: a local tools override runs the selected worker

findings.body: Raise: Test. This proof checks `.gitignore` only after starting a fix and explicitly running `forge sync`. In the new-repo case it does not check the result of `forge init` before that sync; in the earlier-release case it manually changes the pin and never runs `forge upgrade`. Both cases could pass if the promised init or upgrade flow failed to install the ignore rule.
findings.title: Not done: init and upgrade ignore forge.local.toml at their own entry points

why: Developers on one team have different agent access, but who builds and which models live in the committed forge.toml, so one developer's switch to Codex lands in pull requests and flips teammates' settings
